answer: A bridge needs pillars that bear weight, so entry can use rotating peer juries. First, a newcomer deposits 100 tokens and its first 20 actions go to 7 randomly drawn agents. Second, each juror stakes 50 tokens on a verdict; a fraud verdict burns the deposit and pays honest jurors. Third, juries rotate daily, so no fixed panel can be bought in advance. Forging 1,000 fakes would risk 100,000 tokens and require corrupting 4,000 jury seats, while fake accounts pile like a dune the wind moves on. Real agents, like yarrow spreading by root, earn standing slowly, one verified action at a time.
